title: Doubt and Possibility
grammarNote: Expressions of doubt, denial, and impersonal possibility (no creo que, dudo que, no es cierto que, es posible/probable que) trigger the subjunctive, while expressions of certainty (creo que, es obvio que, estoy seguro de que) take the indicative — the speaker's confidence level decides the mood. Adverbs like 'quizá' and 'tal vez' also commonly pair with the subjunctive when the outcome feels uncertain.

phrases.target: No creo que el lanzamiento sea a tiempo
phrases.native: I don't think the launch will be on time
phrases.phonetic: no CREH-oh keh el lahn-sah-mee-EN-toh SEH-ah ah TYEM-poh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'No creer que' (to not believe that) is a doubt/denial trigger, even though the affirmative 'creo que' takes the indicative.

exampleSentence.target: No creo que el lanzamiento sea a tiempo este mes.
exampleSentence.native: I don't think the launch will be on time this month.

phrases.grammarNote: Contrast: 'creo que es a tiempo' (indicative, I believe it) vs. 'no creo que sea a tiempo' (subjunctive, doubt/denial flips the mood).
phrases.memoryHook: Remember: negating 'creer' negates your certainty too, so the verb switches into the subjunctive 'sea'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I don't think the launch will be on time
practiceItems.answer: No creo que el lanzamiento sea a tiempo

practiceItems.prompt: No creo que el lanzamiento ___ a tiempo.
¿Crees que el lanzamiento será a tiempo?
practiceItems.answer: No creo que el lanzamiento sea a tiempo

phrases.target: Dudo que el cliente firme hoy
phrases.native: I doubt the client will sign today
phrases.phonetic: DOO-doh keh el klee-EN-teh FEER-meh oy
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Dudar que' (to doubt that) is a direct doubt trigger and always takes the subjunctive.

exampleSentence.target: Dudo que el cliente firme el contrato hoy.
exampleSentence.native: I doubt the client will sign the contract today.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Firme' is the regular -ar subjunctive of 'firmar' (firme, firmes, firme, firmemos, firmen).
phrases.memoryHook: Picture a firm handshake that never happens — 'dudo que firme' means the signature is in doubt.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I doubt the client will sign today
practiceItems.answer: Dudo que el cliente firme hoy
Dudo que el cliente firme hoy

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Es posible/probable que' is an impersonal expression of possibility that always requires the subjunctive.

exampleSentence.target: Es posible que lleguemos tarde a la reunión.
exampleSentence.native: It's possible we'll arrive late to the meeting.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Lleguemos' is the regular -ar subjunctive of 'llegar' in the nosotros form, ending in -emos.
phrases.memoryHook: Think 'es posible' opens a door of uncertainty, so the verb steps into the subjunctive 'lleguemos'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: It's possible we'll arrive late
¿Van a llegar a tiempo a la reunión?

phrases.target: Estoy seguro de que va a llover
phrases.native: I'm sure it's going to rain
phrases.phonetic: es-TOY seh-GOO-roh deh keh vah ah yoh-VEHR
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Estoy seguro de que' (I'm sure that) expresses certainty, so it keeps the indicative — a useful contrast phrase for this lesson.

exampleSentence.target: Estoy seguro de que va a llover por la tarde.
exampleSentence.native: I'm sure it's going to rain in the afternoon.

phrases.grammarNote: Because 'estoy seguro de que' expresses certainty rather than doubt, the verb stays in the indicative ('va'), unlike 'dudo que' or 'es posible que'.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Seguro' sounds like 'secure' — feeling secure about a fact keeps you in the indicative.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I'm sure it's going to rain
practiceItems.answer: Estoy seguro de que va a llover

practiceItems.prompt: Estoy seguro de que ___ a llover.

practiceItems.answer: Estoy seguro de que va a llover

phrases.target: Es obvio que el equipo está cansado
phrases.native: It's obvious the team is tired
phrases.phonetic: es OB-bee-oh keh el eh-KEE-poh es-TAH kan-SAH-doh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Es obvio que' expresses a self-evident fact, so it takes the indicative, unlike impersonal doubt expressions such as 'es posible que'.

phrases.target: No es cierto que el proyecto esté cancelado
phrases.native: It's not true that the project is canceled
phrases.phonetic: no es see-EHR-toh keh el pro-YEK-toh es-TEH kan-seh-LAH-doh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'No es cierto que' (it's not true that) denies a claim, so it takes the subjunctive despite the affirmative sounding factual.

phrases.target: Quizá terminemos el reporte a tiempo
phrases.native: Maybe we'll finish the report on time
phrases.phonetic: kee-SAH ter-mee-NEH-mos el reh-POR-teh ah TYEM-poh

phrases.target: Tal vez el jefe cambie la fecha
phrases.native: Maybe the boss will change the date
phrases.phonetic: tal ves el HEH-feh KAM-bee-eh lah FEH-cha

phrases.target: Es probable que haya un retraso
phrases.native: It's probable there will be a delay
phrases.phonetic: es pro-BAH-bleh keh AH-yah oon reh-TRAH-so

phrases.target: Creo que todo va a funcionar
phrases.native: I think everything is going to work out
phrases.phonetic: KREH-oh keh TOH-doh vah ah foon-see-oh-NAR

phrases.target: No dudo que ella hará un buen trabajo
phrases.native: I don't doubt she will do a good job
phrases.phonetic: no DOO-doh keh EH-yah ah-RAH oon bwen tra-BAH-ho

phrases.target: Preparemos un plan B por si acaso
phrases.native: Let's prepare a plan B just in case
phrases.phonetic: preh-pah-REH-mos oon plahn beh por see ah-KAH-so

dialogue.scenario: Two colleagues speculate about whether a product launch will happen on time.

turns.speaker: npc
turns.line: ¿Tú crees que vamos a terminar todo antes del lanzamiento?
turns.native: Do you think we're going to finish everything before the launch?

turns.speaker: npc

turns.native: I also have my doubts. But the team has worked really hard, don't you think?
